'''Christopher T. Walsh''' (February 16, 1944 – January 10, 2023) was the Hamilton Kuhn professor of [[biological chemistry]] and [[pharmacology]] at [[Harvard Medical School]].<ref name="Walsh group">{{cite web|url=http://walsh.med.harvard.edu/frame_chris.htm|title=Walsh Laboratory|publisher=Harvard Medical School|accessdate=18 January 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091005085232/http://walsh.med.harvard.edu/frame_chris.htm|archive-date=5 October 2009|url-status=dead}}</ref> His research focused on [[enzyme]]s and [[Enzyme inhibitor|enzyme inhibition]], and most recently focused on the problem of [[antibiotic resistance]].<ref name="duke">{{cite web|url=http://science.medschool.duke.edu/modules/75ann_spks/index.php?id=14|title=Speakers: Christopher T. Walsh, Ph.D.|year=2006|publisher=Duke University Health System|accessdate=18 January 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060909043024/http://science.medschool.duke.edu/modules/75ann_spks/index.php?id=14|archive-date=9 September 2006|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was elected to the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] in 1989.<ref name="duke" />

==Education==
He earned his A.B. degree in biology from [[Harvard University]] in 1965. As an undergraduate, he worked with [[E. O. Wilson]] and published a first-author paper in the journal ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'', where he and his colleagues described the composition of the [[fire ant]] trail substance.<ref name="FireAnt">{{cite journal|doi=10.1038/207320b0|last=Walsh|first=Christopher T. |author2=J.H. Law |author3=E.O. Wilson|year=1965|title=Purification of the Fire Ant Trail Substance|journal=Nature |volume=207|pages=320–321|issue=4994|bibcode=1965Natur.207..320W|s2cid=4265580}}</ref> He went on to graduate school at [[Rockefeller University]], where he earned his Ph.D. in life science in 1970.<ref name="duke" /><ref name="Beeson">{{cite web|url=https://www.princeton.edu/chemistry/macmillan/group-meetings/TDB-walsh.pdf|title=The Career of Christopher T. Walsh|last=Beeson|first=Teresa D. |accessdate=18 January 2010}}</ref><ref name="Harvard2023" />

==Career==
Walsh completed a postdoctoral fellowship with [[Robert Abeles]] at [[Brandeis University]] in 1972, and later that year joined the faculty at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] as a professor of chemistry and biology. In 1987, he joined the faculty at Harvard Medical School to serve as the chair of the newly created Department of Biological Chemistry and Molecular Pharmacology. He served as the president and CEO of the [[Dana–Farber Cancer Institute]] from 1992 to 1995.<ref name="Harvard2023" /> Walsh authored more than 650 publications in scholarly journals and trained several graduate students and postdoctoral researchers.<ref name="duke" /><ref name="Beeson" /> Among his professional activities, Walsh was a member of the Board of Scientific Governors of [[The Scripps Research Institute]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Leadership {{!}} Scripps Research|url=https://www.scripps.edu/about/leadership/?tab-2-text-content=1|access-date=2021-08-31|website=www.scripps.edu}}</ref> the [[American Philosophical Society]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=APS Member History|url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=Christopher+Walsh&title=&subject=&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced|access-date=2021-08-31|website=search.amphilsoc.org}}</ref> [[The National Academy of Sciences]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Member Directory |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/christopher-t-walsh-jtidvs/ |publisher=National Academy of Sciences |access-date=17 October 2022}}</ref> [[Institute of Medicine]], [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], and the [[American Academy of Microbiology]].

==Personal life==
Walsh was born in Boston and went to [[Roxbury Latin School]]. Walsh died following a fall on January 10, 2023, at the age of 78. He was married to [[Diana Chapman Walsh]] who was the president of [[Wellesley College]] from 1993 to 2007. They have one daughter, [[Allison Kurian]], a professor of medicine and epidemiology at Stanford University.<ref name="Harvard2023">{{cite web | title=Christopher T. Walsh Dies | website=Harvard Medical School | date=2023-01-11 | url=https://hms.harvard.edu/news/christopher-t-walsh-dies | access-date=2023-01-12}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Oldach |first1=Laurel |title=Biochemist Christopher T. Walsh dies at 79 |journal=[[Chemical & Engineering News]] |date=January 13, 2023 |url=https://cen.acs.org/people/obituaries/Biochemist-Christopher-T-Walsh-dies-at-79/101/web/2023/01 |access-date=27 February 2023}}</ref>
